video_title: Crypto Crashes as Anthropic Pulls Off the Biggest IPO Ever
gist: Bankless weekly roundup: Bitcoin loses its 200-week moving average amid six competing sell-off narratives (macro, AI unwind, Anthropic IPO liquidity drain, miner selling) while gold and MSTR/STRC also crack; the hosts frame Jensen Huang's Nvidia ouster as capitalists vs. statists, dissect the record ~$1.7T Anthropic IPO (hypergrowth, aggressive unlocks, P(doom) as a 'put'), and review Coinbase-ChatGPT trading, Backpack's CFTC license, Kalshi's Utah charges and Solana Breakpoint.

themes.theme: Crypto capitulation: Bitcoin loses the 200-week MA

insights.claim: Bitcoin fell about 12.5% over seven days and sits roughly 8% below its 200-week moving average (~68K), matching the depth below that average seen at the mid-2025 ~56K bottom.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Distance below the 200-week MA is the key regime gauge; watch whether it widens toward FTX-like levels.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is 8% below its 200 week, which was which is currently as much down below its 200 week as it was during the 56,000 bottom

insights.claim: Bitcoin has printed seven consecutive red weekly candles, something that has happened only two or three times before in its history, in what looks like a liquidation cascade.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Rare streaks like this tend to cluster near capitulation; useful as a contrarian timing input.
insights.quote: Bitcoin's at seven weeks, seven red uh weekly candles in a row, which has only happened like two or three times before in Bitcoin's history.

insights.claim: Michael Nato calls this the third capitulation since the 10/10 crash (after February and June); key levels are the 50-week MA at 75K (lost), the 200-week MA at 68K (lost), the June low at 58K (holding), and a 'basement' at the on-chain realized price of about 53K.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Map of support levels: 58K June low then ~53K realized price are the levels to watch for further downside or bottom-buying.

insights.claim: If Bitcoin falls to the ~53K realized price it would be about 22% below its 200-week MA, which is FTX-level territory without an FTX-type event, and would signal a structural break of Bitcoin's long-term trend.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: A break below 58K/53K would invalidate long-term trend models; treat it as a regime-change signal rather than a dip.

insights.claim: Sentiment is at extremes: the fear and greed index hit a 9-month low, more fearful than at the June 58K low, and Crypto Twitter sentiment is described as worse than post-FTX.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Sentiment worse than at a lower price level is a classic contrarian bottoming signal.
insights.quote: Crypto Twitter sentiment is worse than post FTX.

insights.claim: ETH is down about 12% on the week to around $1,778, below $1,800, tracking Bitcoin, with Solana, altcoins and Zcash all lower.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Correlation is near one across crypto; no relative-strength hiding place among majors.

insights.claim: The weekend featured extremely aggressive, price-insensitive Bitcoin selling with no bounces, prompting questions about whether a large seller knows something.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Price-insensitive flow suggests forced or informed selling; watch for identification of the seller.
insights.quote: Some of the most aggressive price insensitive Bitcoin selling I've ever seen in my entire

insights.claim: David argues the current bear cycle is less severe than FTX, reflected in Bitcoin being only ~8% rather than ~25% below its 200-week MA, though he felt the prior early-bull phase seemed too easy.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Frames the drawdown as a cyclical washout rather than systemic failure unless deeper levels break.
insights.quote: It's not as bad as FTX and that's reflected in the fact that we are at the bottom

insights.claim: Absent a black swan, what would send Bitcoin meaningfully lower is a true AI bubble pop, such as a ~50% Nasdaq selloff, rather than the current retrace to April levels.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Crypto downside is now tied to AI-equity tail risk; Nasdaq drawdown depth is the leading indicator.

insights.claim: One explanation for the crypto sell-off is macro tightening: CPI keeps printing hot, the dollar is rising, and talk of renewed Fed hiking echoes Michael Howell's call that a liquidity-shrinking 'turbulence era' favors bonds over risk assets.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: If liquidity is the driver, watch the dollar, CPI and Fed pricing rather than crypto-native catalysts.

insights.claim: A second explanation is the AI trade unwinding: Nasdaq/QQQ is down about 13-14% back to April levels and Nvidia's sharp drop may have triggered margin calls in Asia and reflexive capital flight from risk assets including crypto.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Crypto is trading as a high-beta AI-risk proxy; Nvidia is a key cross-asset tell.

insights.claim: A third explanation is retail selling crypto to fund purchases of the Anthropic IPO, with analysts pointing to a ~30% Bitcoin dump right before the SpaceX IPO as precedent.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Mega-IPOs can drain retail liquidity from crypto; expect pressure around future large listings.

insights.claim: Other narratives include a hidden seller or blown-out margin linked to the earlier Binance hack (CZ denies Binance is selling) and general chaos such as bank outages, FAA groundings, cyberattacks and 'normie' prepping.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Opaque tail risks keep a fear premium on crypto; watch for forensic explanations.

insights.claim: Michael Nato points to a spike in Bitcoin miner selling from late October into November as the match that lit the sell-off, as buyers who wanted in had already bought in September-October and could not absorb the excess supply.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Track miner outflows/balances as a supply-side signal for BTC bottoms.

insights.claim: Eight of the ten largest publicly traded Bitcoin miners now have AI hosting contracts, so miners behave like neoclouds and may sell BTC to fund the more valuable neocloud buildout or out of AI-trade jitters.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Miner treasuries are now a structural source of BTC supply tied to AI capex; monitor miner AI pivots.
insights.quote: eight of 10 of the biggest publicly traded uh miners, they all have AI hosting contract deals

insights.claim: David's view is that all the narratives are simultaneously true, which is why prices are where they are.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: No single catalyst to fade; recovery likely needs several headwinds to ease.
insights.quote: I think it's all true, dude. It's all true and that's why prices are what they are.

insights.claim: Gold is down about 33% from its January high and silver about 60%, so the debasement trade has failed alongside Bitcoin; Luke Gromen called the gold crash uglier than Bitcoin's.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Debasement hedges are not diversifying crypto in this drawdown; correlation regime has shifted.
insights.quote: Gold down 33% from the January high earlier this year. Silver down 60%.

insights.claim: Strategy's STRC preferred is trading about 5-6% off its $100 peg (~$95) and MSTR is around $85-87, selling off as hard as anything else.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: STRC peg deviation is a stress gauge for the Bitcoin treasury-company model.

insights.claim: The S&P 500 is making new local lows faster than the Nasdaq, an unusual pattern where the Nasdaq holds up while the S&P breaks down.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Breadth deterioration beyond tech suggests a broader risk-off rather than a pure AI unwind.

insights.claim: Stan Druckenmiller says he is neither long nor short equities at current prices.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: A top macro investor sitting flat signals limited conviction on equity upside.
insights.quote: We are not long equities. We're not short equities

themes.theme: Pockets of strength: Pearl, Derive, Venice, NEAR Intents

insights.claim: Pearl, a roughly one-year-old chain pitched as a quantum-safe store-of-value alternative to Bitcoin that uses AI inference for mining, rose about 63% on the week after Ryan Watkins' fund published a Pearl thesis.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: New 'AI + store of value' narratives can rip in down markets on concentrated fund theses; beware crowded thesis posts.

insights.claim: At a ~$4.5B market cap versus Zcash's ~$15B, David considers Pearl 'very rich' and impossible to underwrite as a one-year-old store of value, and will not buy it.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Fade or avoid young store-of-value tokens priced near established privacy/SoV assets.
insights.quote: It's inherently impossible to underwrite like a $4.5 billion one-year-old asset that's going to be a store of value money

insights.claim: Pearl's most liquid market is on NEAR Intents rather than Coinbase or Kraken, a notable case of a decentralized solver network beating centralized exchanges on execution for a standalone L1 asset.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Evidence of cross-chain intent networks capturing order flow from CEXs; bullish signal for NEAR Intents usage.

insights.claim: During the capitulation, options platform Derive had its busiest fee week and highest fee day ever, though its token sold off anyway, while Venice hit all-time highs in daily VVV burn.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Revenue-generating tokens decoupling from price during sell-offs can be value opportunities; track fees vs. price.

insights.claim: David frames Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia as capitalists versus statists: free-market tech elites want him back, while China-hawk national security officials (Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent) view Nvidia as a defense company and reportedly drove his removal over chip sales to China.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Chipmakers now carry political/defense-contractor risk; China exposure can trigger state intervention.

insights.claim: Jensen publicly said he would be honored to return as Nvidia CEO, backed by tech CEOs and the All-In hosts calling for a shareholder vote, but the Nvidia board, which owns few shares, said it is not interested.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Board-shareholder misalignment is a governance catalyst; a shareholder push or return could re-rate NVDA.
insights.quote: I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO to Nvidia.

insights.claim: Nvidia stock is down about 30% since Jensen's ouster, which the hosts read as the market's verdict on wanting him back.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: A Jensen return is a potential upside catalyst for NVDA.

insights.claim: Ryan, citing Ben Thompson's 'Obituaries' piece, likens the episode to China's Jack Ma takedown and expects Jensen may return but chastened and reined in, marking a shift from free-market tech to 'political tech'.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Expect US tech leaders to align more with national-security priorities, constraining China sales and open-weight strategies.

insights.claim: David argues the perceived extralegal removal of a tech leader, a violation of due process like the Jack Ma playbook, is an understated cause of one of the worst US tech sell-offs ever in the following ten days.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Rule-of-law risk premium on US tech is rising; watch Jensen's congressional testimony.

insights.claim: David places Anthropic in the statist camp: Dario has warned Congress against open-weight models while Jensen promoted them, and Anthropic paid $1.6 million to lobbying firms tied to Marco Rubio and Susie Wiles.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Anthropic may be a political-winner beneficiary in a state-aligned AI regime, unlike open-weight advocates.
insights.quote: Anthropic paid $1.6 million to two lobbying firms tied to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wilds.

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO: valuation, unlocks, and P(doom)

insights.claim: Anthropic's IPO is the largest ever, about 25% bigger than SpaceX's; it priced around $83, opened above $110 and traded around $96 on day one at roughly $1.7 trillion fully diluted, while the S&P and Nasdaq fell.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Strong debut amid a down tape shows deep demand for frontier-AI exposure.

insights.claim: Anthropic's revenue grew from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024 and $4.6 billion in 2025, to $81 billion now, roughly 10x a year for four years, making it the fastest-growing revenue company ever.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Hypergrowth underpins the valuation; sustainability of growth is the key underwriting question.

insights.claim: Anthropic is a low-float stock with aggressive unlocks: about 7.2% unlocked now, ~300 million employee shares sellable on day one, heavy unlocks over the first six months and no locked shares within a year.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Unlock-driven supply overhang may pressure the stock over the next 6-12 months, crypto-style.

insights.claim: Anthropic's seven co-founders are each worth at least $20 billion, about 600 employees will hold $100 million and 2,800 will hold $1 million out of roughly 5-6 thousand staff, an extreme wealth concentration.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Concentrated employee wealth plus unlocks creates potential selling pressure and a new angel-capital wave.

insights.claim: Under new Nasdaq fast-entry rules, Anthropic will join the Nasdaq-100 within about 15 trading days, so QQQ holders will own roughly $8 per $1,000 by December.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Index inclusion creates forced passive buying in December.

insights.claim: David says the Jensen/Nvidia episode reframing AI labs as defense companies made him reconsider his earlier view that Anthropic, unlike SpaceX, lacked uniqueness given OpenAI and Chinese labs.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: State-aligned AI labs may earn monopoly-like positioning; changes the competitive moat analysis.

insights.claim: Paul Christiano's April 2023 predictions on Bankless (AI transforming industry, agents arriving, agents learning to cheat, models detecting and evading oversight, lab coordination failing) have all come true, and he now puts about 10% odds on an AI takeover within a year.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: AI-safety forecasters' track record argues for pricing tail risk into AI exposure.
insights.quote: there's nothing to suggest that they're wrong and their track record of prediction has been on the ball.

insights.claim: The hosts reason that buying Anthropic is like buying a put on AI doom: if recursive self-improvement takes off, Anthropic could 5x from $1.7 trillion, and true doom cannot be hedged anyway, so expected value favors buying; Ryan remains undecided.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Frames frontier-lab equity as a hedge against AI disruption of all other assets.
insights.quote: buying anthropic feels like buying a put

themes.theme: Exchange convergence, AI trading, and regulatory clashes

insights.claim: Coinbase now lets US users trade crypto, stocks and futures directly from ChatGPT, and Ryan expects every brokerage, including Robinhood, to follow as AI agents become a personal CIO from strategy to execution.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: Agentic, headless trading could shift brokerage competition to AI integrations.

insights.claim: The CFTC granted Backpack DCM and DCO licenses, making it the first exchange with blockchain-based order execution to join the short list of CFTC-licensed venues like Coinbase, Kraken and Kalshi.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: On-chain execution is gaining US regulatory legitimacy; watch onshore perps competition.

insights.claim: Variational raised a Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation as an RFQ-style brokerage/aggregator rather than an order-book exchange, part of a convergence of perps, prediction markets and exchanges like Hyperliquid and Lighter into super apps.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Exchange categories are collapsing into super apps; differentiation shifts to execution and distribution.

insights.claim: Kalshi's co-founders were summoned to a Utah criminal court on 13 felony counts tied to state gambling law even as federal regulators and the CFTC approve of Kalshi, highlighting a states-versus-federal clash over prediction markets.
insights.speaker: Ryan (co-host)
insights.so_what: State-level legal risk is a live overhang for prediction-market businesses despite federal clearance.

themes.theme: Solana Breakpoint and the money-vs-revenue barbell

insights.claim: At Breakpoint, Mert argued SOL should be valued as money/store of value, while Anatoly has consistently called SOL an anti-spam token, which David sees as an incredibly bearish value-capture framing.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Leadership ambivalence on SOL's monetary role weakens the value-accrual thesis.

insights.claim: The Solana Foundation became majority owner of CoinGecko, which David reads as a distribution play for Solana apps and tokens, something the Ethereum Foundation would never do.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Solana is acting like a company buying distribution; signals a corporate-style growth strategy.

insights.claim: Solana dropped its mainnet-beta label for protocol version 1.0, and an ICE-owned NYSE alternative trading system said it can accept Solana-minted tokens and may run a Solana validator; Zel also picked Solana for Zel USD, which Ryan predicts will flop.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: TradFi venue integration supports Solana tokenization adoption.

insights.claim: David says SOL is not investable: for revenue he would buy Hyperliquid, Lighter, Derive, Venice or pump tokens, and for undervalued store of value he would buy Bitcoin, Ether or Zcash; SOL is stuck in the money/revenue barbell, as ETH was last cycle.
insights.speaker: David (co-host)
insights.so_what: Barbell framing: own revenue tokens or SoV assets, avoid L1s in the middle.
insights.quote: If I wanted to buy revenue, I will buy Hyperlquid Lighter Derive Venice. one of these pump tokens.
